dossier.purpose: Ollama is a Go local-LLM runtime and model manager. `ollama serve` runs an HTTP server (default 127.0.0.1:11434) that pulls models from registry.ollama.ai, schedules them onto CPU/GPU, and serves native /api/* endpoints plus OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings) and Anthropic-compatible (/v1/messages) endpoints. GGUF models run through a supervised upstream llama.cpp `llama-server` subprocess; safetensors models run through an in-tree MLX engine. `ollama launch` configures coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI and others) to use that server. Relevant to the stated needs: it is a local model server with embedding endpoints (/api/embed, /api/embeddings, /v1/embeddings). A repo-wide search found no OTLP receiver or exporter, no metrics/log/trace store, no dashboard, no dataset/experiment store, and no code-indexing or semantic-search feature (see telemetry_and_network and risks).

claims.claim: macOS and Linux install with `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh` (macOS alternatively a manual Ollama.dmg download); Linux manual-install instructions are on docs.ollama.com/linux
'The official Ollama Docker image `ollama/ollama` is available on Docker Hub.'
Official client libraries are ollama-python and ollama-js (separate repositories); `pip install ollama` and `npm i ollama` examples are given
Running `ollama` prompts you to run a model or connect Ollama to existing agents/applications such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Codex, Copilot and more
`ollama launch claude` launches a specific integration; supported integrations include Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, DeepSeek Harness, Droid and OpenCode (OpenClaw via `ollama launch openclaw`)
`ollama run gemma4` chats with a model; the full model list is at ollama.com/library
'Ollama has a REST API for running and managing models'; example POST http://localhost:11434/api/chat; all endpoints are documented at docs.ollama.com/api
Supported backends: llama.cpp (the only backend listed)
Documentation links: CLI reference, REST API reference, importing models, Modelfile reference, building from source (docs/development.md)
Community 'Observability & Monitoring' integrations (third-party projects): Opik, OpenLIT ('OpenTelemetry-native monitoring for Ollama and GPUs'), Lunary, Langfuse, HoneyHive, MLflow Tracing
Community 'Database & Embeddings' integrations (third-party): pgai, MindsDB, chromem-go, Kangaroo; RAG/knowledge-base projects (RAGFlow, R2R, MaxKB and others) are listed separately
The README makes no statement about telemetry, privacy, authentication or hardening; a 'Security proxy for Ollama' (Ollama Fortress) appears only as a community project

platforms.macos_arm64: yes - docs/macos.mdx:5-8 (macOS 14+, Apple M-series CPU and GPU); docs/gpu.mdx:136-139 (Metal); docs/development.md:21,122 (macOS arm64 builds Metal inference, MLX on by default). platforms.gpu: yes for NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (compute capability 8.9) - docs/gpu.mdx:5-6,18 (compute 5.0+, driver 550+); the CUDA 12 payload arch list includes 89 and the CUDA 13 payload includes 89-virtual (llama/server/CMakePresets.json:71,103); driver-floor logic in discover/cuda_compat.go:10-19,64-72; Linux release bundles carry cuda_v12/cuda_v13 dirs (release.yaml:682). If nvidia-smi is missing on bare-metal Linux the installer adds NVIDIA's CUDA repo and installs cuda-drivers (scripts/install.sh:313-451); with nvidia-smi present it stops after install (scripts/install.sh:294-297).

integrations.mcp: none found - no MCP server or client code in this repo (a grep for MCP matches only integration-config tests and comments); docs only point to an external Python MCP server for Ollama web search that lives in the ollama-python repo (docs/capabilities/web-search.mdx:310-312).
integrations.sdk_or_api: HTTP API, default http://127.0.0.1:11434 (envconfig/config.go:20-24): native /api/{generate,chat,embed,embeddings,tags,show,ps,pull,push,create,copy,delete,version,status}, OpenAI-compatible /v1/{chat/completions,completions,embeddings,models,responses,audio/transcriptions} and Anthropic-compatible POST /v1/messages (server/routes.go:2020-2074; docs/api/introduction.mdx:13-25). integrations.claude_code_or_codex: yes - `ollama launch claude` runs Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at the local server (docs/integrations/claude-code.mdx:9-15; cmd/launch/claude.go:52-87); manual env-var setup at claude-code.mdx:191-209; headless `--yes` requires --model (claude-code.mdx:114-122; cmd/launch/launch.go:487). `ollama launch codex [--config|--restore]` writes ~/.codex/ollama-launch.config.toml and model.json and runs `codex --profile ollama-launch` (docs/integrations/codex.mdx:18-37,59-78; cmd/launch/codex.go:54-81,211-338) and requires Codex >= 0.134.0 (codex.go:781); `codex --oss` is the manual path (codex.mdx:39-57). Also macOS Claude Desktop and ChatGPT/Codex desktop-app connectors (docs/integrations/claude-desktop.mdx; cmd/launch/registry.go:55-67,97-108) and a loopback-only Codex gateway route /api/codex on the server (server/routes.go:2025-2027).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry SDK, analytics beacon, OTLP exporter/receiver, Prometheus endpoint or metrics store exists in the repo: a grep for otel|OTLP|opentelemetry|prometheus|/metrics|sentry|posthog|mixpanel|amplitude|datadog matches only README.md:326 (third-party OpenLIT listing) and unrelated tests/comments; go.mod:5-91 has no such modules; the route table server/routes.go:2020-2074 has no /metrics or OTLP paths (the comment at :2161-2168 mentions net/http/pprof but nothing in the repo imports it). docs/faq.mdx:159-161 says local runs do not send prompts/data to ollama.com and describes cloud processing; docs/cloud.mdx:88-92 repeats it. Outbound traffic found in code: (1) model pulls/pushes go to registry.ollama.ai by default (types/model/name.go:38-43) with User-Agent ollama/<ver> (<arch> <os>) Go/<ver> (server/images.go:1413) and redirects allowed to ollama.com, ollama.ai, hf.co, huggingface.co (server/images.go:1380). (2) On `ollama serve` start the server runs two background cloud caches (server/model_caches.go:17-27; routes.go:2157): model recommendations fetched from https://ollama.com/api/experimental/model-recommendations at start and every ~4h with jitter, 3s timeout (server/model_recommendations.go:23-37,151-233), and cloud model-info hydration via ollama.com /api/tags + /api/show (server/model_show_cache.go:123-131,335-392,444-497); requests are signed with the local ed25519 key ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 (server/cloud_proxy.go:372-385) which `ollama serve` creates if missing (cmd/cmd.go:2101-2163), and carry X-Ollama-Client-Version. All of this is skipped when cloud is disabled via OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json (envconfig/config.go:237-238,382-385,440-449; internal/cloud/policy.go:11-17; docs/faq.mdx:163-181). (3) `:cloud` models and web search/fetch are proxied to https://ollama.com:443 (override OLLAMA_CLOUD_BASE_URL) and need an Ollama account or API key (server/cloud_proxy.go:28-32,59-72,74-137; docs/api/authentication.mdx:7-34; docs/capabilities/web-search.mdx:9-11). (4) Windows/macOS desktop app only (build tag windows||darwin): hourly GET https://ollama.com/api/update with os, arch, version, timestamp, nonce, signature and, on macOS, a device UUID; the check is unconditional, only the download is gated by the auto-update setting (app/updater/updater.go:1,32-36,53-101,388-405; app/store/store.go:251-259). (5) A loopback-only Codex Desktop gateway at /api/codex forwards non-Ollama models to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex or https://api.openai.com/v1 and appends one line per request (route, model, method, path, status, duration, result; no bodies) to ~/.ollama/logs/codex-proxy.log (server/codex_proxy.go:13-34; internal/proxy/codex_desktop.go:28-30,157-176,481-516). Source builds fetch llama.cpp, MLX, mlx-c and xgrammar from GitHub at configure time (llama/server/CMakeLists.txt:181-184; cmake/mlx/CMakeLists.txt:65-68). Logging: slog text logs to stderr (logutil/logutil.go:14-33; server/routes.go:2098) plus gin access logs (routes.go:2012), journald on Linux and ~/.ollama/logs/server.log on macOS (docs/troubleshooting.mdx:6-16); llama-server runs at --log-verbosity 4 (llm/llama_server.go:575-582). OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS=1 writes full request bodies plus curl replay scripts to an OS temp dir for /api/generate, /api/chat, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses and /v1/messages (server/inference_request_log.go:33-55,112-124; routes.go:2054-2074). Claude Code/Codex telemetry: `ollama launch claude` appends env vars (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1, DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1, ...) to the inherited environment, and a test asserts DISABLE_TELEMETRY and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC are not set (cmd/launch/claude.go:63,67-87; claude_test.go:370-375); there is no OTEL_* handling anywhere in the repo, the Codex launcher only writes its own profile/catalog files (cmd/launch/codex.go:77-79,211-338), and only the Claude Desktop profile writer sets disableEssentialTelemetry/disableNonessentialTelemetry=true (cmd/launch/claude_desktop.go:741-759).

code.architecture: Single Go module github.com/ollama/ollama (go.mod:1-3). main.go -> cmd/ (cobra CLI). server/ is the gin HTTP server: routes.go (native /api/*, OpenAI /v1/*, Anthropic /v1/messages), sched.go (model scheduler), images.go/download.go/upload.go/create.go (registry pull/push/create), cloud_proxy.go (proxy to ollama.com for :cloud models), model_caches.go/model_recommendations.go/model_show_cache.go (background cloud caches), inference_request_log.go (opt-in request-body logging). llm/ starts and talks to a `llama-server` subprocess on 127.0.0.1 for GGUF models (llm/server.go:98-111; llm/llama_server.go:350-443). llama/server and llama/compat hold the CMake wrapper that FetchContent-pulls llama.cpp (pinned by LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b11081) and applies an Ollama compatibility patch layer (llama/compat/README.md:3-10). mlx/, mlxrunner/ and cmake/mlx implement the MLX engine for safetensors models (default on macOS arm64, optional CUDA 13; docs/development.md:120-131). discover/ does GPU discovery (CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal). openai/, anthropic/ and middleware/ translate the compatibility APIs onto the native chat path. api/ is the Go client and wire types; envconfig/ holds env-var configuration; cmd/launch/ holds agent integrations; internal/proxy holds the Claude/Codex Desktop gateways; app/ is the desktop GUI (Go + React) with updater. cmd/bench is a benchmark tool and integration/ holds end-to-end tests.
code.packaging_and_release: Tag-triggered .github/workflows/release.yaml (push of v* tags, :3-6) builds: macOS arm64 app/zip/dmg/tgz, signed with an Apple identity and notarized (scripts/build_darwin.sh:175-286; release.yaml:29-94); Windows installer and zips signed via Google Cloud KMS/signtool (release.yaml:399-477; scripts/build_windows.ps1:1020-1044); Linux per-arch .tar.zst bundles (ollama-linux-<arch>.tar.zst plus -rocm, -jetpack5/6 and -mlx variants) built through Docker buildx (release.yaml:479-710, archives made at :701-705); multi-arch Docker images pushed to vars.DOCKER_REPO (release.yaml:712-745; scripts/tag_latest.sh:7-13 defaults to ollama/ollama and re-tags latest/rocm via .github/workflows/latest.yaml). The release job uploads artifacts plus install.sh and a sha256sum.txt manifest (release.yaml:748-860; checksum generation :788-790); the GitHub release is first created as draft+prerelease (:830-834). No cosign/GPG/SLSA attestations were found; Docker builds set provenance: false and sbom: false (release.yaml:543-544,637-638,657-658). Version and release mode are stamped with ldflags (release.yaml:25). Third-party licenses (llama.cpp, cpp-httplib, MLX, xgrammar) are packaged alongside (llama/server/CMakeLists.txt:618-634; cmake/mlx/CMakeLists.txt:138-169).
code.tests_and_ci: Go testing with testify/go-cmp (go.mod:9,15): 353 *_test.go files, 29 of them in integration/ behind the `integration` build tag (integration/README.md:5-11), the rest are unit tests across server/, cmd/, cmd/launch/, model/, mlxrunner/, app/ and others; 22 Vitest UI test files under app/ui/app/src (package.json:15-18). cmd/bench is a throughput/TTFT benchmark CLI; no benchmark results are published in the repo. CI in .github/workflows: test.yaml (pull_request only, ignoring docs/README, :13-18) runs native superbuilds for Linux (CPU, CUDA 13 with arch 87 only, ROCm 7.2, Vulkan, MLX CUDA 13; :81-176) and Windows (CPU, CUDA 13, ROCm 7.1, Vulkan, MLX CUDA 13; :177-369), `go mod tidy --diff` (:370-375), a Go dependency-license check when go.mod changes (:377-392), `go generate` plus `go test -count=1 -bench=. -benchtime=1x ./...` on ubuntu/macos/windows with golangci-lint (:394-461), UI `npm test` on ubuntu (:431-434) and `go test -race` on ubuntu/macos (:463-501); a patches job verifies llama.cpp patches apply (:62-79). test-install.yaml runs scripts/install.sh on ubuntu/macos when it changes; test-llamacpp-update.yaml builds unsigned artifacts when LLAMA_CPP_VERSION changes; test-xgrammar.yaml runs on macOS; release.yaml and latest.yaml are release-only. Lint config is .golangci.yaml. No scheduled workflows, CodeQL, or dependabot config found under .github.
code.dependencies: Go: go.mod has 76 requires = 31 direct + 45 indirect, `go 1.26.0` (go.mod:3-91). Notables: gin v1.10.0 and gin-contrib/cors (HTTP), cobra v1.7.0 (CLI), bubbletea/lipgloss (TUI, cmd/tui), mattn/go-sqlite3 (desktop app store and onboarding state, CGO), klauspost/compress (zstd), golang.org/x/crypto (ed25519 key), tree-sitter (only used by mlx/generator). No OpenTelemetry, Prometheus or vector-DB modules. UI: app/ui/app/package.json has 20 dependencies and 38 devDependencies (React 19, TanStack, Vite 6, Vitest, Storybook), lockfile app/ui/app/package-lock.json. Native: llama.cpp pinned by LLAMA_CPP_VERSION (b11081) and fetched from github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp at CMake configure time (llama/server/CMakeLists.txt:115-117,181-184); MLX pinned by MLX_VERSION (59d600b5e64c238427d0f8d897ab7c682ef4d3d2) and mlx-c by MLX_C_VERSION (ebc88f10caa1b625e6b581437a8dea6df8a70085, mlx/CMakeLists.txt:23-28); xgrammar v0.2.7 (cmake/mlx/CMakeLists.txt:65-68).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: report vulnerabilities privately by emailing hello@ollama.com (SECURITY.md:5-7) and give time before public disclosure; lists user best practices (update, secure hosted instances, monitor; :15-21). No response SLA, disclosure timeline, advisory process or supported-versions table is stated. CONTRIBUTING.md:13 routes security issues to it.

claim_checks.claim: docs/faq.mdx:159-161 - 'We don't see your prompts or data when you run locally'
claim_checks.evidence: No analytics/telemetry SDK or OTLP exporter exists in the code (see telemetry_and_network); llama-server is bound to 127.0.0.1 with --offline (llm/llama_server.go:372-377). But a default `ollama serve` still contacts ollama.com for model recommendations and cloud model info (server/model_recommendations.go:23-26,188-205; server/model_show_cache.go:123-131,335-392), the desktop app checks for updates hourly (app/updater/updater.go:33-35,388) and pulls go to registry.ollama.ai (types/model/name.go:39). Server-side handling is not checkable from this repo.

True for the binary (envconfig/config.go:20-24; cmd/cmd.go:2106), but the Docker image sets OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 (Dockerfile:332) and the server has no authentication (docs/api/authentication.mdx:5); OLLAMA_AUTH (envconfig/config.go:231-232) is only read by the Go client (api/client.go:119,184). The Host-header check is skipped when bound to a non-loopback address (server/routes.go:1941-1951).

claim_checks.claim: docs/faq.mdx:25 - 'By default, Ollama uses a context window size of 4096 tokens'
claim_checks.evidence: Code wins: when OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is unset (api/types.go:1143) the server picks a VRAM tier: 262144 for >=47 GiB, 32768 for >=23 GiB, otherwise 4096 (server/routes.go:129-131,2199-2209; envconfig/config.go:338; docs/context-length.mdx:8-12). The 4096 statement holds only for <23 GiB or CPU; a 24 GB-class card falls in the 32768 tier (comment at routes.go:2200).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:323-330 - Observability and monitoring (including OpenTelemetry-native monitoring) is offered via community integrations
claim_checks.evidence: Consistent with the code: the repo itself has no OTLP/OpenTelemetry/Prometheus support - grep for otel|OTLP|opentelemetry matches only README.md:326; go.mod:5-91 has no such modules; server/routes.go:2020-2074 has no /metrics or OTLP routes. These integrations are external projects, not native features.

risks: Scope: no OTLP receiver/exporter, metrics/log/trace store, dashboards, dataset/experiment store or code-indexing/semantic-search layer in this repo - `otel|OTLP|opentelemetry` appears only in README.md:326 (third-party listing), go.mod:5-91 has no OpenTelemetry/Prometheus/vector-DB modules, server/routes.go:2020-2074 has no /metrics or OTLP routes. Observability is limited to per-response usage fields (docs/api/usage.mdx:5-15), text logs, /api/ps and /api/status (routes.go:2297-2305,2422-2454). Embedding endpoints exist (routes.go:2056-2057,2065) but nothing indexes or queries code; replay-style tooling is only cmd/bench (throughput/TTFT, benchstat/CSV) and opt-in request-body logging.

Privacy/network: default `ollama serve` makes outbound calls to ollama.com even for local use (model recommendations every ~4h and cloud model-info hydration at startup, signed with the local ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 key; server/model_recommendations.go:23-26,188-205; server/model_show_cache.go:335-392; server/cloud_proxy.go:372-385; cmd/cmd.go:2101-2163). OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD only covers cloud features (envconfig/config.go:332,440-449). The Windows/macOS desktop app always checks https://ollama.com/api/update hourly, sending os/arch/version and (macOS) a device UUID; only the download honors the auto-update setting (app/updater/updater.go:33-35,53-101,388-405; app/store/store.go:251-259).

Security: the local API has no authentication (docs/api/authentication.mdx:5; docs/api/anthropic-compatibility.mdx:383); the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 (Dockerfile:332) and the Host-header filter only applies when bound to loopback (server/routes.go:1948-1951); default CORS origins include localhost, 0.0.0.0, app://, file://, tauri://, vscode-webview:// (envconfig/config.go:85-109). OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS=1 writes full request bodies and curl replay scripts to an OS temp dir (server/inference_request_log.go:33-47,112-124). SECURITY.md gives only an email contact, no SLA.

Supply chain: the documented install is `curl | sh` (README.md:15-17,31-33) and scripts/install.sh streams the tarball into tar without checksum or signature verification (install.sh:129-157). Releases publish only a sha256sum.txt (release.yaml:788-790,859); no cosign/GPG/SLSA attestations, Docker builds set provenance: false and sbom: false (release.yaml:543-544,637-638,657-658). Windows and macOS binaries are code-signed (scripts/build_windows.ps1:1020-1044; scripts/build_darwin.sh:247-286); Linux tarballs are not.

Maintenance/dependency chain: pre-1.0 (v0.35.0); API 'isn't strictly versioned' (docs/api/introduction.mdx:55-57). GGUF inference depends on a pinned llama.cpp tag (b11081) fetched from GitHub at configure time and patched by an Ollama-maintained compat layer that its own README calls temporary (LLAMA_CPP_VERSION:1; llama/server/CMakeLists.txt:181-184; llama/compat/README.md:3-10); llama/README.md:5-9 warns a bump can affect model loading, GPU discovery and scheduling. A second engine (MLX, pinned commits MLX_VERSION/MLX_C_VERSION, xgrammar v0.2.7) is also in tree.

Docs drift: docs/faq.mdx:25 (4096 default context) contradicts the VRAM-tiered default in code (server/routes.go:2199-2209); docs/troubleshooting.mdx:46-60 still describes cuda_v11/rocm_v5/cpu_avx2 libraries while presets build cuda_v12/cuda_v13 (llama/server/CMakePresets.json:56-111); the server comment at routes.go:2161-2168 says DefaultServeMux is used 'so we get net/http/pprof for free' but nothing in the repo imports net/http/pprof, so whether pprof endpoints are exposed was not verified.

Integration coupling: `ollama launch codex` requires Codex >= 0.134.0, rewrites ~/.codex/ollama-launch.config.toml and model.json, and may edit ~/.codex/config.toml to remove legacy entries (cmd/launch/codex.go:211-338,270-298,781). `ollama launch claude` appends env vars (DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1, CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0, ...) to the inherited environment, and a test asserts DISABLE_TELEMETRY and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC are deliberately not set (cmd/launch/claude.go:63,67-87; claude_test.go:370-375); Ollama does not configure or filter Claude Code/Codex OTEL telemetry. The Anthropic endpoint is a subset: no count_tokens, tool_choice, metadata, prompt caching, batches, citations or PDF (docs/api/anthropic-compatibility.mdx:387-400).

Platform: the RTX 4090 path relies on bundled CUDA 12/13 payloads and NVIDIA driver >=550 (docs/gpu.mdx:6; discover/cuda_compat.go:14-18). WSL2 is supported only as Linux with NVIDIA passthrough and needs systemd for the service (scripts/install.sh:243-262); there is no dedicated WSL2 doc page. The Linux installer needs sudo and zstd and, when nvidia-smi is absent, adds NVIDIA repos and installs cuda-drivers and kernel headers (install.sh:138-143,313-451). CI only builds CUDA payloads (test.yaml:93-97); GPU/model integration tests are not run by any workflow (integration/README.md:5-11).
